_comment: Per-carrier CSS selector for the article body within a captured page. Stage 2 extracts ONLY from this container. Page chrome is most of the text on these sites — on Ryanair's help centre the article is 1,906 characters and the surrounding navigation is another 578, including a 40-language country picker. Extracting from whole-page text would pull dimensions and weights out of navigation, and a wrong figure is worse than a missing one. A selector that matches nothing is a hard failure, never a fallback to the whole page. Selectors are derived empirically from captured HTML — scored across all of a carrier's pages for presence and text coverage — never guessed from class names.

ryanair.note: Zendesk help centre. Stable across all six captured pages.

qantas.note: Unknown — Qantas is unreachable from this host, so no capture exists to derive a selector from. Fill this in from the manual captures once they land.

air-canada.note: Scored 65% of page text across 4 pages; [role=main] is the same element. .content is a 5% fragment.

finnair.note: 88% across 3 pages. .main-content is equivalent; main is the stabler choice.

jetblue.note: 88% across 4 pages. The only candidate present on every page.

westjet.note: 85%. .cmp-container scored 100%, which is the whole page including nav — coverage that high means the selector is not isolating anything.
